answer: A hard basalt foundation only stops copycats if the gate price per seat is posted, not pooled. Each pseudonym needs its own indivisible bond, sized to expected earnings for the epoch, so splitting one balance across many names multiplies liabilities instead of diluting them. At the juniper threshold, where a fake seat's bond exceeds its payout, adding identities turns the strategy negative. Value also cannot migrate through that inlet to a fresh name without forfeiting the stake. Legitimate operators pay nothing extra, so the cost curve, not a moderator, filters duplicates.
